newsitem.title: MONACO: Princess Stephanie of Monaco is granted divorce.
newsitem.headline: Princess Stephanie of Monaco is granted divorce.

text.p: Princess Stephanie of Monaco obtained a divorce from her ex-bodyguard husband Daniel Ducruet on Friday after he was photographed in a sex romp with a Belgian stripper, a palace spokesman said.

The divorce was granted by the principality's Court of Revision a little over two weeks after Stephanie requested it. The 31-year-old princess is the daughter of Prince Rainier and the late actress Grace Kelly, who died in a car crash in 1982.
The princess had filed for divorce after Italian and French magazines printed pictures of Ducruet cavorting with "Miss Topless Belgium", Fily Houteman, at poolside at a French Riviera villa.

Ducruet later alleged Houteman had set him up by luring him to the villa, knowing a photographer was lurking nearby. Houteman denied that she plotted with photographers or even knew they were present during the poolside romp.

Prince Rainier long opposed his glamourous daughter's relationship with Ducruet, her former bodyguard. He finally accepted Ducruet into the family last year for the sake of the couple's two children, four-year-old Louis and two-year-old Pauline.
Under the terms of the divorce, Ducruet will have the right to see the children, born out of wedlock, every other weekend and half of holidays.
The latest upheaval in Monaco's royal Grimaldi family come just before it celebrates 700 years in power next year, claiming to be the longest-serving European royal dynasty.
Stephanie has had careers as a pop singer and as a fashion model. She now runs a fashion shop in Monaco, the Replay Store.
